sightings.summary: A glowing green object was observed by hundreds of witnesses across Moscow, described as a bright fireball moving across the evening sky.
sightings.description: In early 2025, hundreds of residents across Moscow observed a glowing green object traversing the evening sky. The object was described as a bright fireball-like phenomenon, distinctly green in color, moving at considerable speed. Multiple witnesses captured video footage on their phones. The event generated significant discussion on Russian social media. No official explanation was provided by authorities, though some speculated it could be a bolide (bright meteor) or space debris re-entry. The green coloration is notable — green fireballs have been historically associated with both natural bolide events and unidentified aerial phenomena.
sightings.ref: Russian sightings compilation; social media reports

sightings.location: Sosnovy Bor, Leningrad Oblast (near nuclear power plant)
sightings.summary: An unidentified object was spotted near the Leningrad Nuclear Power Plant. Russian military confirmed it was not a drone or airplane — "the object moved at the speed of wind with no engines." Fighter jets were scrambled.
sightings.description: On approximately April 5, 2023, an unidentified flying object was spotted near Russia's Leningrad Nuclear Power Plant in the city of Sosnovy Bor in the Leningrad Oblast. Russian military officials investigating the incident stated to TASS that they were certain it was not a drone or an airplane: "The unknown object moved at the speed of the wind. This means it doesn't have engines, which means it isn't a drone or an airplane." Local media reports over Telegram indicated the object was located at 10,000 meters altitude and moving at 200 km/h. Fighter jets were reportedly scrambled and airspace was briefly closed. The Leningrad Oblast Deputy Governor Mikhail Ilyin later stated the information about the UFO "wasn't true," contradicting earlier military statements. The proximity to a nuclear facility elevated the security concerns significantly. The Leningrad Oblast is far from Ukraine, bordering Estonia and Finland, ruling out conflict-related drones.
sightings.ref: Jerusalem Post Apr 7, 2023; TASS; RIA Novosti

sightings.summary: Russian air defenses reportedly shot down a UFO in Rostov Oblast near the Ukrainian border. Authorities dismissed it as a drone but could not confirm its identity.
sightings.description: In early January 2023, Russian air defenses reportedly shot down an unidentified flying object in the Rostov Oblast, near the Ukrainian border along the Sea of Azov. The identity of the object remained unclear. Russian lawmaker Anatoly Wasserman claimed it was a Ukrainian drone, given the proximity to the conflict zone. However, military officials could not definitively identify the object. The incident occurred during heightened tensions and increased aerial surveillance along the Russia-Ukraine border.
sightings.ref: Jerusalem Post Apr 2023; Russian state media

sightings.summary: The Moscow Pyramid: a large triangular or pyramid-shaped craft was filmed hovering motionless over the Kremlin for several minutes by multiple independent witnesses.
sightings.description: In December 2009, multiple independent witnesses filmed a large, dark, triangular or pyramid-shaped object hovering motionless in the sky directly above the Kremlin in central Moscow. The object appeared to rotate slowly on its axis. Videos were uploaded from at least two different vantage points, showing the same object from different angles, which reduced the likelihood of a single-source hoax. The Russian media covered the sightings, though official authorities did not comment. The object was estimated to be quite large based on its apparent size relative to the Kremlin buildings below it. Some analysts suggested it could be a reflection or atmospheric phenomenon, but the consistency across multiple videos from different locations made this a widely discussed case internationally.
sightings.ref: Multiple YouTube videos; Russian media coverage; international press

sightings.summary: Scientists investigated a field in Perm Oblast where a UFO had reportedly landed, leaving a circular impression 62 meters in diameter.
sightings.description: Komsomolskaya Pravda of October 12, 1989, reported that a group of scientists had visited a field in Perm Oblast to investigate claims that a UFO had landed in that area and had left behind a circular impression measuring 62 meters in diameter. The investigation confirmed the presence of the ground depression, though the nature of what created it remained disputed.

sightings.summary: Military officer Maj. V. Loginov officially reported a massive luminous sphere over Omsk visible at several kilometers altitude, moving at 7,000 km/h. Radar could not detect it despite visual confirmation by pilots.
sightings.description: On October 21, 1989, Sotssialisticheskaya Industriya reported that hundreds of residents in Omsk had observed a UFO, with many eyewitnesses reporting directly to the newspaper's office. The article included an authoritative military report by Maj. V. Loginov, who stated: "I must tell you straight off that radar did not detect this object, and so I am reporting visual observations." The object was passing over at an altitude of several kilometers. The visible shining sphere appeared to be about one and a half kilometers in size, shaped like the moon in the night sky. Four projectors cast very bright beams, some parallel and some at angles to the Earth. The object was in the field of vision for about 5 minutes, hovering over the civil airport before descending slightly. Then the projectors were turned off and a whirling plume trail instantaneously appeared. The object began to recede rapidly northwest to east. Pilots from a neighboring airport were able to observe it visually but could not detect it on their radar screens — radar signals could not be reflected from it. Colleagues in the Altay Kray region reported the object flew toward them and they had it under visual observation within 5 minutes, meaning it had covered approximately 600 kilometers at a speed of about 7,000 kilometers per hour. According to Loginov, all observations indicated that the object was controlled by intelligence.

sightings.summary: Russia's most famous close encounter: TASS reported a UFO landing in a city park with 9-foot tall, three-eyed aliens and a robot companion. Investigated by police, scientists, and covered by international media.
sightings.description: On September 27, 1989, at approximately 6:30 PM, children playing football in Yuzhny Park near the Vostok movie theater in Voronezh witnessed a glowing pink light that became a deep red ball approximately 9 meters (30 feet) in diameter. The object descended and landed in the park. According to over 40 witnesses, including children and adults, a hatch opened and beings emerged — described as approximately 9 feet tall with small heads, bronze-colored skin, three eyes, and silvery overalls with bronze boots. One wore a disk-like device on its chest. They were accompanied by a robot-like figure. One being allegedly used a tubular weapon to make a boy vanish temporarily before the crowd's eyes. The beings walked through the park before re-entering the craft and departing. The Soviet state news agency TASS officially reported the incident on October 9, 1989, stating scientists had confirmed the landing and found traces including ground depressions matching a craft weighing several tons, elevated phosphorus levels 100x above baseline, doubled radiation, and two rocks of unknown composition. Lt. Sergei Matveyev of local police confirmed he personally observed the craft's descent. Children drew consistent depictions of a banana-shaped craft with an X symbol when isolated from each other. The Voronezh Geophysical Laboratory under Genrikh Silanov led the investigation. Sightings continued between September 21 and October 2. The incident remains Russia's equivalent of the Roswell case.
sightings.ref: FBIS/CIA DOC_0005517761; TASS; Wikipedia; TIME Magazine Oct 1989; ThinkAboutItDocs; Black Vault

sightings.summary: Physical scientist Elvir Kurchenko investigated a circular depressed area in a forest near Surgut, where a worker claimed a UFO had visited the site.
sightings.description: Stroitelnaya Gazeta of September 16, 1989, reported that physical scientist Elvir Kurchenko had begun investigating another circular depressed area in a forest near Surgut in Western Siberia. A worker at the site claimed that a UFO had visited the location. The investigation was part of a broader wave of UFO reports across the Soviet Union during the summer and fall of 1989.

sightings.summary: Engineer Yuriy Ponomarenko and workers at a collective farm reported a disk-shaped UFO with two beams of light emanating from its sides, observed on the ground for 20 minutes with no sound.
sightings.description: Sotssialisticheskaya Industriya of July 25, 1989, reported that a UFO sighting had been claimed by engineer Yuriy Ponomarenko and a group of workers at a collective farm in the Dnepropetrovsk region. The object was described as a disk with two beams of light emanating from its sides. The witnesses maintained that they had observed the object on the ground for about 20 minutes, and that it emitted no sound when it flew away.

sightings.summary: Hundreds of residents witnessed a 450-foot jellyfish-shaped UFO that reportedly split into multiple green lights over the city.
sightings.description: In 1989, hundreds of witnesses in Nalchik, the capital of the Kabardino-Balkarian Republic in the North Caucasus, observed a massive object estimated at 450 feet in size. The object was described as jellyfish-shaped, reminiscent of the Petrozavodsk phenomenon twelve years earlier. According to witnesses, the object eventually split into several distinct green lights that moved independently before disappearing. The event caused significant alarm among the local population.
sightings.ref: Russian sightings compilation; multiple media sources

sightings.summary: Soviet military aircraft encountered a large flying disk that directed beams at the cockpit. Both crew members became invalids; the aircraft commander died within months from radiation-related cancer.
sightings.description: Soviet military official Anatoliy Listratov reported an encounter between a Soviet aircraft and a UFO over the city of Borisov. The crews of two Soviet aircraft reported seeing a large flying disk in their vicinity with five beams of light emanating from it — three directed toward the ground and two projected upward. The ground controller instructed one plane to alter course and approach the object, at which point the disk flew to the same level and aimed one of its beams at the approaching Soviet plane, illuminating the cockpit. The aircraft commander was at the controls; the copilot observed the maneuver and was able to raise his hand to shield himself from the unbearable light. The aircraft commander was resting in the adjoining seat, and a bright ray of light projected a spot with a diameter of 20 centimeters across his body. Both pilots felt heat. According to Listratov, the aircraft commander and his copilot both became "invalids" shortly after the incident. The copilot was forced to leave his job due to sudden deterioration in health including prolonged periods of loss of consciousness. The aircraft commander died within a few months. The cause of death was listed as "cancer" and "injury to the organism as a result of radiation from an unidentified flying object" was listed as a contributing factor on the official medical record at the hospital where he died.

sightings.summary: A flying sphere crashed into Hill 611 near Dalnegorsk. Scientists from the USSR Academy of Sciences recovered unusual metallic debris including gold, silver, nickel, alpha-titanium, and mesh of 17-micron threads.
sightings.description: On January 29, 1988, many observers saw a flying sphere crash into one of the twin peaks of Hill 611 near the village of Dalnegorsk in Primorsky Krai. Physicists and other scientists from the Siberian Division of the USSR Academy of Sciences investigated the site and found remarkable physical evidence. Scientist A. Makeyev reported finding gold, silver, nickel, alpha-titanium, molybdenum, and compounds of beryllium at the crash site. The debris included fine mesh with threads of only 17 microns in diameter, twisted into braids with extremely thin gold wires intertwined — described as evidence of intricate technology beyond present terrestrial science by Dr. V. Vysotskiy of the Chemical Sciences department. Small spherical glass-like objects were also recovered. Skeptical physicists from Tomsk hypothesized the sphere could have been a "plasmoid" formed by geophysical force fields, but other researchers rejected this theory since the metal concentrations at the site exceeded atmospheric levels by a factor of 4,000. The event remains under investigation and is considered one of the most physical-evidence-rich UFO cases in Russian history.
sightings.ref: FBIS/CIA DOC_0005517761; RusArtNet; CIA Reading Room

sightings.summary: The Petrozavodsk Phenomenon: a massive jellyfish-shaped luminous object appeared over the city at 4 AM, emitting thin ray-like beams of light toward the ground. Caused panic, affected electronic equipment, and left holes in glass windows.
sightings.description: On September 20, 1977, at approximately 4:00 AM, residents of Petrozavodsk witnessed a massive bright object in the sky, described as jellyfish-shaped or like a luminous medusa. The object emitted thin, intense rays of light directed downward toward the city. Witnesses reported that the phenomenon caused widespread panic. Local electronic and technical equipment experienced interference and malfunctions during the event. Notably, circular holes were reportedly found in apartment windows after the event, as if the glass had been melted through. The phenomenon was observed for approximately 10-12 minutes before the object moved westward toward Lake Onega and disappeared. The event was covered extensively in Soviet media and prompted scientific investigation. Some researchers have attributed the phenomenon to a rocket launch from the Plesetsk Cosmodrome, though this explanation does not account for all reported effects, particularly the glass damage and equipment interference.

sightings.summary: A UFO crashed on Zelyony Island south of Rostov-on-Don. Wreckage was confiscated by NKVD troops overnight. Rare chemical elements later found at the site.
sightings.description: In June 1941, just before the German invasion, a UFO allegedly crashed into the island of Zelyony, south of Rostov-on-Don. The wreckage was removed at night in trucks and the island was cordoned off by NKVD troops — the secret police initially believed it to be a German spy plane. The pieces of the object were taken to Rostov and then to Kapustin Yar (later a major Soviet rocket test site), where they subsequently disappeared. In the 1980s, rare and abnormal chemical elements were found on the island during geological surveys, suggesting the crash debris had unusual material composition.

sightings.summary: A cylindrical craft emitting flames crashed through the frozen surface of Lake Vedlozero. A strange creature was seen on shore. Anomalous electromagnetic effects persist in the area to this day.
sightings.description: In November 1928, a cylindrical craft emitting flames fell into Lake Vedlozero near the village of Shuknavolok in Karelia. The craft struck the ice of the frozen lake and sank into the water. For a while, the object could be seen about 70 centimeters below the surface. A year later, the object mysteriously vanished. Witnesses on the shore reported seeing a strange creature with thin arms and legs, which immediately dived back into the water upon being seen. The area experienced a series of anomalous events: in 1932, a dense black cloud descended on the village and left a gel-like substance on the ground, which peasants collected in bottles and used as a healing substance. To this day, interference affects television sets in Shuknavolok, but not in the surrounding area. In the 1980s, a Mi-8 military helicopter arrived with divers to try and locate the object, but they were unsuccessful.

sightings.summary: Locals witnessed the explosion of a cigar-shaped UFO near Karpinsk in the Ural Mountains.
sightings.description: In 1927, locals witnessed the explosion of a cigar-shaped UFO near the town of Karpinsk in the Urals. The object was described as elongated and metallic before it detonated in mid-air. Details of any debris recovery are not documented in available sources.

sightings.summary: Workers in St. Petersburg observed a shining metal apparatus that slowly moved across the sky for approximately 20 minutes.
sightings.description: In 1912, workers in the Nevskaya Zastava district of St. Petersburg observed a "shining metal apparatus" which slowly moved across the sky for around twenty minutes before disappearing from view. The following year, 1913, there were mass reports of strange airships in the night-time skies from towns as far afield as Kiev, Izmail, Kazan, and Perm. These sightings predated any known Russian aviation capability of that scale.

sightings.summary: Massive aerial explosion flattened 2,150 square kilometers of Siberian forest. No impact crater found. Cause remains debated — meteor, comet, or unknown.
sightings.description: The Tunguska Event is the largest impact event on Earth in recorded history. At approximately 7:14 AM local time, an explosion occurred near the Podkamennaya Tunguska River in Siberia, flattening an estimated 80 million trees over 2,150 square kilometers. The explosion is estimated at 10-15 megatons of TNT — about 1,000 times the energy of the Hiroshima bomb. Witnesses hundreds of kilometers away reported seeing a bluish-white column of light nearly as bright as the sun, followed by a flash and a thunderous sound. The shockwave knocked people off their feet and broke windows at distances of up to 60 kilometers. Despite the enormous power, no impact crater was ever found, which remains one of the central mysteries. While commonly attributed to a meteor or comet airburst, the absence of a crater and the unusual tree-fall pattern have made this event a persistent subject of alternative theories, including in Russian UFO literature.
sightings.ref: Multiple scientific sources; RusArtNet; Russian Academy of Sciences

sightings.summary: Reports across the entire Russian Empire of strange oval objects floating in the sky during spring 1892.
sightings.description: In spring 1892, there were reports all over the Russian Empire of strange oval objects floating in the sky. The sightings were widespread and occurred across multiple cities and regions simultaneously, suggesting either a single large phenomenon or coordinated observations of the same type of object. No official investigation records survive from this period.

sightings.summary: A massive 40-meter flaming sphere hovered over Lake Robozero for two hours, witnessed by an entire parish congregation during the Feast of the Assumption.
sightings.description: The most famous UFO case in ancient Russian history, recorded by monks of the St. Cyril of Belozersk Monastery. From the north, out of a clear sky, appeared a huge flaming sphere no less than 40 meters in diameter — the height of a modern 15-storey building. From its fore part emitted two flame beams about 40 meters ahead of it; from its sides poured bluish smoke. The sphere hovered over the lake as worshippers emerged from church, terrified. They prayed with tears and weeping, and the object vanished. It reappeared twice more, each time dimmer, moving westward before disappearing entirely. The event lasted approximately two hours. Fishermen in a boat on the lake reported the water below the object became illuminated to the bottom, and the heat was so intense they could not approach. Fish fled to the banks.
sightings.ref: St. Cyril of Belozersk Monastery chronicles; ThinkAboutItDocs; RusArtNet
